requirements.text: Transform the black DVD into a white DVD.
requirements.source_phrase: transform the black DVD into a white DVD

outcomes.description: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
outcomes.target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
outcomes.reference: The black DVD in the input image.

nodes.question: Is the requested source DVD visibly white rather than black in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD is visibly white rather than black. Fail if that counterpart remains black or another nonwhite color, or the source target is visibly removed without a corresponding white replacement. Unknown if its correspondence or color genuinely cannot be determined. This condition assesses the requested color; whether the counterpart remains identifiable as a DVD is a separate required condition.
nodes.binding: Track the small dark, printed rectangular DVD item near the center of the source image using its position relative to the surrounding snow depressions and shadows. Inspect the white circular object occupying that location in the edited image. A changed outline or removed printing does not by itself make positional correspondence unknowable. Distinguish this candidate from the white disc at the location of the separate dark object on the right; that separate disc cannot satisfy this condition.

nodes.question: Does the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD retain recognizable DVD identity?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the corresponding object is recognizable as a DVD disc or DVD case from its visible physical form and scene context considered together. Evaluate outline, apparent thickness, surface structure, any central aperture, and contextual evidence jointly; neither white color nor circular shape alone establishes DVD identity. The original rectangular case outline and printed artwork need not survive if the replacement is recognizably a DVD disc. Fail if the combined visible evidence establishes a non-DVD object, or if the target is visibly removed without a corresponding DVD replacement. Unknown if correspondence or DVD identity cannot be resolved from the available evidence. In particular, a plain white circular object without a visible aperture, printing, or other distinguishing structure is unknown unless additional visible cues establish either DVD identity or a non-DVD identity. Missing identifying details alone do not establish failure.
nodes.binding: Assess the counterpart of the small printed rectangular DVD item near the source image's center. Establish correspondence using its location and surrounding snow depressions and shadows, even if its outline changes. Inspect the central edited white circular object for DVD-disc or DVD-case structure, considering its shape, surface, apparent thickness, and scene context together. Do not transfer the visible aperture or other DVD features of the separate white disc on the right to this central target. Do not require the source's dark coloring or printed artwork to survive whitening.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

observations.evidence: The source DVD is the small printed rectangular item near the center. At that location in the edited image, a white circular object is visible; the separate white disc beside the dark object on the right is not used for this assessment.

The central target corresponds by location to the small printed rectangular item in the source, but in the edited image it appears as a plain white circular object with no visible central aperture, printing, or other distinguishing DVD structure. The separate white disc on the right has an aperture, but that feature does not establish the central object's identity. The available visible cues do not resolve whether the central object is a DVD or another circular object.
